candidates.title: Intermodal rail powers up with 7% gain for latest week
candidates.excerpt: Rail traffic on U.S. carriers came to 535,663 carloads and intermodal units, up 4.9% compared with the same week last year, according to Association of American Railroads data for the week ending Sept. 19. Total carloads reached 234,207 units, up 2.4%, while intermodal volume was 301,456 containers and trailers, better by 6.9% compared to 2025. Seven of the 10 carload commodity groups posted an increase compared with the same week in 2025. Metallic ores and metals surged 15.1%, followed by petroleum and petroleum products, 12.5%, and nonmetallic minerals such as sand and stone, 7%. Grain paused its long stretch of gains, down 7.7%, joined by losses in coal, 3.1%, and motor vehicles and parts, 0.8%. Through the first 37 weeks of the year, U.S. railroads reported cumulative volume of 8,444,095 carloads, up 2.7%, and 10,477,086 intermodal units, up 4.1%, y/y. candidates.title: Tropical Shipping raises South Florida drayage charges
candidates.excerpt: Tropical Shipping will increase drayage charges for full-container-load cargo moving to or from selected locations in South Florida. The revised charges will take effect on 18 October 2026. Tropical Shipping attributed the adjustment to rising fuel costs. Each affected charge will increase by US$50. The revised inland transportation charges apply to FCL cargo originating from or destined for the listed counties, cities and communities.

candidates.title: RCL launches new weekly China to Indonesia service
candidates.excerpt: Regional Container Lines and its partners will launch a new weekly service connecting China with Indonesia. The service, branded RCI05, will connect three major Chinese gateways with Jakarta and Surabaya before calling Singapore. The port rotation will be: Qingdao – Shanghai – Nansha – Jakarta – Surabaya – Singapore – Qingdao The complete rotation will take 28 days. RCI05 weekly schedule The maiden voyage is scheduled to depart Qingdao on 8 November 2026. Vessels deployed on the service will range in capacity from 2,800 to 4,300 TEU. RCL said the inclusion of Qingdao, Shanghai and Nansha will provide coverage across North, East and South China, offering customers wider market access and greater routing flexibility. The Singapore call will also provide connections to RCL’s broader regional and international network.

candidates.title: Yang Ming and OOCL eye Suez Canal return as carrier traffic increases
candidates.excerpt: Yang Ming and OOCL are considering further moves back to the Suez Canal, while COSCO plans additional transits as major container lines gradually increase their use of the waterway. The developments were discussed during a meeting between Suez Canal Authority (SCA) Chairman Admiral Ossama Rabiee and representatives of 20 major shipping lines and agencies on 23 September. According to the SCA, Yang Ming is seriously considering returning to the Canal in the near future. OOCL also intends to return, with an experimental transit expected during October. COSCO plans additional Suez transits COSCO is also considering increasing its voyages through the Canal following the recent successful transit of one of its affiliated container vessels. Hany El-Sallamy, General Manager at COSCO, said three additional vessels affiliated with the shipping line are scheduled to transit the Canal in the coming period. candidates.title: Port of Oakland recorded export surge
candidates.excerpt: The Port of Oakland handled 173,818 TEUs in August 2026, with full exports increasing 2.9% from July. Combined loaded cargo totalled 131,666 TEUs, down 9% compared to August 2025, while empty container volume reached 42,152 TEUs, down 11.4% year-on-year. The port recorded 82 vessel calls in August, compared to 90 in the same month last year. Year-to-date loaded cargo is down 2.5 percent, with full imports declining 4.6 percent partially offset by full exports up 0.2 percent. Empty container movements are down 11.4 percent year-to-date. Acting Maritime Director Jason Garben described loaded cargo volumes as remaining relatively stable year-to-date, with exports slightly ahead of last year, and expressed focus on building on that foundation through closer engagement with ocean carriers, shippers and terminal partners to identify growth opportunities and attract more customers to the Oakland gateway.

candidates.title: CMA CGM introduces China to East Africa peak season surcharge
candidates.excerpt: CMA CGM will introduce a Peak Season Surcharge for shipments from China to Dar es Salaam in Tanzania and Mombasa in Kenya. The surcharge will take effect on 15 October 2026 and remain applicable until further notice. For shipments originating in China, the surcharge will be subject to filing with the Shanghai Shipping Exchange and may be incorporated into the ocean freight rate.

Hapag-Lloyd has cut contracted capacity allocations under its Quality Freight Product (QFP) service by as much as 40%, according to one forwarder, raising questions over the flexibility of the carrier’s guaranteed-capacity offering amid the disruption in Asia. candidates.excerpt: Navios tied to four boxship newbuilds in South Korea Angeliki Frangou-led Navios Maritime Partners has been linked to another four containership newbuilds at South Korea’s HJ Shipbuilding & Construction (HJSC), in a deal worth around $500m. HJSC disclosed this week that it had signed up an unidentified Oceania-based owner for four containerships, with the contract worth KRW679bn ($500m) running from September 21, 2026 through April 30, 2029. The shipbuilder did not disclose the vessels’ capacity or propulsion specification. Shipbuilding and market sources have, however, identified Navios as the buyer, with the contract pricing pointing to ships of around 10,100 teu. That would take Frangou’s business at HJSC into a larger size class. Navios has been a repeat customer at the Busan yard, initially building up a series of 7,900 teu methanol-ready, scrubber-fitted ships before adding four 8,850 teu newbuilds linked to the same builder. candidates.title: Private credit steady as private equity rebounds
candidates.excerpt: Private credit steady as private equity rebounds Private credit remained steady in the second quarter of 2026, while private equity rebounded, according to new research by index provider MSCI. The MSCI Global Private Credit Closed-End Fund Index gained 1.7 per cent in the second quarter, up from 0.9 per cent in the first quarter, the firm said. candidates.title: Importers push back on CBP supply chain data proposals
candidates.excerpt: Importers push back on CBP supply chain data proposals Hapag-Lloyd champions IoT container telemetry but importers – and factory data – highlight practical flaws of mandatory paper trails. US Customs and Border Protection’s (CBP) proposal to mandate heightened supply-chain data disclosures to boost cargo security is drawing sharp pushback from importers. While ocean carriers see an opportunity to leverage advanced technology, importers warn that foreign paper trails are often non-existent – a gap highlighted by recent data straight from Chinese factory hubs. In response to proposals in an Advance Notice of Proposed Rulemaking issued by CBP earlier this month, ocean carrier Hapag-Lloyd urged the agency to move beyond traditional paper declarations. Bill Stephens of Trains Magazine breaks down what Grupo Mexico Transportes is doing differently: winning volume from highway and short-sea moves, expanding rail ferry capacity, and using a more aggressive security strategy to cut cargo theft incidents. If you move freight across North America, this is a real look at where rail competition is shifting. #RailFreight #CargoTheft #MexicoLogistics Grupo México Transportes, the largest railroad in Mexico, has ordered two additional rail ferries capable of carrying 150 railcars each across the Gulf of Mexico, according to rail journalist Bill Stephens, who visited the company’s headquarters in Guadalajara this week. The expansion comes as demand on the joint-venture ferry service — operated with Genesee & Wyoming — outpaces capacity and volumes surge on finished-vehicle shipments manufactured in Mexico.
